name: Getac ZX70-EX
statusNote: No longer in Getac's range, which now lists the ZX80-EX; no end-of-sale notice.
summary: The Getac ZX70-EX is the hazardous-area version of a Getac rugged 7-inch tablet, certified for Zone 2/22 under IECEx. Getac also states ATEX certification, but the certificate isn't published. It is an intrinsically safe (Ex ic) design running Android 10. It has been discontinued; the Getac ZX80-EX replaces it.

atex.marking: II 3G Ex ic op is IIC T5 Gc / II 3D Ex ic op is IIIB T100°C Dc
atex.status: IECEx Current, issue 5, checked 2026-10-25; ATEX not published

iecex.marking: Ex ic op is IIC T5 Gc / Ex ic op is IIIB T100°C Dc

certification.protection: Intrinsic safety (Ex ic) with inherently safe optical radiation (op is)

safety.conditions: Ambient −21 to +60 °C; controlled environment with reduced pollution; protect from UV and impacts with high impact energy; not next to strong charge-generating processes; the ATEX hand strap TF1-STRAP and the anti-static display film must be installed for any use in hazardous locations; follow the manufacturer safety instructions.
safety.peripherals: Certificate does not list a connection-interface ban. Rubber I/O cover is a certified accessory and must be fitted; DC-in, USB host and micro-USB client ports are not for use in hazardous areas (assumed, not in the certificate text).
safety.certifiedAccessories: Named in the certificate: hand strap (ATEX hand strap TF1-STRAP is mandatory), shoulder strap, rotating hand strap, wrist strap, capacitive stylus and tether, anti-static film (mandatory), rubber I/O cover. AC adapter not for hazardous areas.

specs.ports: DC-in, USB 2.0 host, micro-USB client, microSD; optional barcode imager, HF RFID/NFC
specs.touch: Capacitive multi-touch; glove-enabled per standard model

unconfirmed.safety.charging: Not stated in the certificate. The battery isn't user-removable, and later Getac Ex tablets forbid charging in the zone.
unconfirmed.safety.batterySwap: Not stated in the certificate. The battery isn't user-removable, and later Getac Ex tablets forbid charging in the zone.
unconfirmed.safety.peripherals: Not stated in the certificate; based on the rubber I/O cover it lists as an accessory.
unconfirmed.os.securityUntil: Getac's date for the standard model; Getac lists no separate date for the EX version.
unconfirmed.launchYear: Approximate: the maker doesn't publish a launch date. Based on the certificate date or the maker's announcement.

strengths: Among the lightest Zone 2 tablets of its size we list, at 774 g in use
Certified for ambient temperatures up to +60 °C
limitations: Discontinued; the Getac ZX80-EX replaces it
Zone 2 only, so not for Zone 1 areas
T5 temperature class: fine for most gases, but not those that ignite below 100 °C
Dust group IIIB: combustible flyings and non-conductive dust only, not conductive dust
